extracted.intended_audience: newsroom editors, journalists, and media professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing BuzzFeed's Editorial Standards and Ethics Guide: a set of policies and norms for newsroom behavior, sourcing, on- and off-line conduct, and treatment of sensitive material. Useful for newsroom staff and editors implementing or comparing editorial ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: On the deletion of stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial posts should never be deleted for reasons related to their content, or because a subject or stakeholder has asked you to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy forbids content removal for content-related reasons or external requests; preserves editorial independence and archival record.

rubrics_metrics.name: On paying for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not pay sources for interviews. If an interview incurs costs to a source through travel or work compensation lost, we may be able to reimburse them, but check with your editor before agreeing to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default: no payment for interviews. Reimbursement of incurred costs is possible but requires editor approval to avoid conflicts or appearance-of-bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: On providing advance questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Giving a subject a general sense of the direction of the interview is fine, but we should decline to provide questions to subjects in advance of an in-person interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing a general sense of topic is acceptable; do not hand over specific questions before in-person interviews to preserve spontaneity and rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: On the use of graphic content
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally speaking, we will embed or link to the graphic content we are writing about. We have technical tools that give our readers the opportunity to opt in to view graphic content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer embedding or linking rather than auto-displaying graphic material; use technical measures so readers must opt in to view graphic content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profanity: Swearing is OK
rubrics_metrics.description: We speak the language of the internet — which is often hilarious and often profane. As such, profanity is permitted on BuzzFeed; but see the BuzzFeed Style Guide for more information on how to style it responsibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profanity is allowed when appropriate to audience/voice, but staff should consult the style guide for guidelines on styling and responsible use to avoid gratuitous or harmful language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t snap selfies with celebrities
rubrics_metrics.description: Selfies are fantastic and you should take them as often as possible with friends and loved ones. But when celebrity visitors come to a BuzzFeed office, please don’t ask for photographs unless the staffer who brought them in has checked that it’s OK.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff should avoid asking visiting celebrities for photos unless cleared by the hosting staffer; respects guest boundaries and organizational protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: On public activism
rubrics_metrics.description: But when it comes to activism, BuzzFeed editorial must follow the lead of our editors and reporters who come out of a tradition of rigorous, neutral journalism that puts facts and news first. If we don’t, it makes it harder for those reporters to do their jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial staff should prioritize neutral, fact-based reporting and follow editor guidance on activism to avoid undermining newsroom credibility and colleagues' reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: On political speech
rubrics_metrics.description: While we understand that many BuzzFeed editorial staffers are passionate and thoughtful and hold personal views on policy issues or candidates, we must maintain one blanket rule for all of editorial: Political partisanship may not be expressed in public forums, including Twitter and Facebook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees in editorial roles must refrain from expressing partisan political views in public forums/social media to maintain perceived impartiality of the newsroom.

rubrics_metrics.name: On potential conflicts of interest (investors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our investors have no influence on our reporting, and reporters should not take any special note of investors’ views or interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters must avoid letting investors' views or interests influence coverage or decision-making; maintain separation between editorial work and investor interests.
